newsitem.title: USA: N. Dakota wheat gets needed rain but still suffers.
newsitem.headline: N. Dakota wheat gets needed rain but still suffers.

text.p: Scattered showers brought much-needed moisture to North Dakota during the week ended Sunday, but overall soil moisture levels declined, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

Condition of all crops deteriorated during the week despite the rain. Fifty-four percent of the spring wheat crop rated good or excellent, against 66 last week. Sugarbeet condition dropped considerably to 66 percent good to excellent, against 86 last week and 84 percent a year ago.
Topsoil moisture was rated 73 percent short to very short, against 69 in that category last week, 17 percent last year and the average of 25 percent.
Spring wheat was 95 percent emerged, ahead of 87 last week, 89 last year and the five-year average of 94 percent.
Durum wheat was 94 percent emerged versus 76 a week ago, 85 a year ago and 91 percent average. Eleven percent was jointing versus one percent a week ago and four percent a year ago and 22 average.
Oats were 93 percent emerged, up from 84 a week ago, 89 a year ago and the same as 93 percent average.
Barley emerged was 96 percent vs 88 percent a week ago, 91 percent a year ago and 94 percent average.
Corn was 95 percent emerged, compared with 84 percent a week ago, 93 a year ago and 93 percent average.
Soybeans were 92 percent emerged compared with 61 percent a week ago, 76 a year ago and 87 percent average.
Sugarbeets emerged totaled 97 percent versus 97 percent a week ago, 99 percent a year ago and 99 average.
Sunflowers were 79 percent emerged compared with 46 a week ago, 68 a year ago and 75 percent average.
